dish: Galley Boy — double cheeseburger with Swen RED and Swen WHITE sauces, speared with a pimento olive; curb-hop service
w: Pop Swenson started selling burgers from his station wagon at Buchtel High in 1933 and opened this South Hawkins drive-in in 1934; it's still the flagship of Akron's signature burger, the Galley Boy, run to your car by sprinting curb-hops. Signal Akron readers' Best Burger 2025; Beacon Journal readers' bracket winner 2026; Reader's Digest's best burger in Ohio.

dish: Frozen custard — vanilla, chocolate and the flavor of the day, from Bill Strickland's low-air batch freezer
w: Bill and Florence Strickland opened this walk-up stand in 1936 on the same spot it still occupies; Bill, an Akron Pure Milk man, built his own batch freezer to keep air out of the custard. A spring-to-fall Akron ritual and a WKYC top-15 Northeast Ohio ice cream pick.

dish: The Bittner — 3/4 lb of vanilla ice cream blended with house chocolate syrup, topped with double-buttered, double-salted pecans
w: Canton's ice-cream parlor since 1926, with its old fountain and booths; the Bittner, invented in 1931 and named for a delivery boy, is the order — a spoon-standing shake-sundae hybrid you eat, not drink.

dish: Fresh seafood flown in from Boston (Foley's Fish) and prime beef, in the mahogany-and-tile 1902 barroom
w: Canton's oldest restaurant (1902), in the Jacob family since 1932 — it survived Prohibition and a 1988 fire, and George Halas and Jim Thorpe dined here the week the NFL was formed in 1920. On the Canton Repository foodie panel's 11 best in Stark County.

dish: Thin, crisp-crust pizza with the semi-sweet sauce, and the cheesy Luigi's salad
w: Downtown Akron's Italian landmark since 1949 (Ciriello family), its brick entry papered with signed celebrity photos and a line out the door late at night. Signal Akron readers' Best Pizza 2025; No. 1 pizza and No. 1 Italian in Akron Life's 2026 330 Flavor Awards.

dish: Pad see ew, red curry and fresh sushi rolls
w: Thai-born owner Charlie Somtrakool opened Cilantro in 2009 after a friend said Akron lacked good Thai food; Signal Akron readers named it Akron's Best Restaurant in 2025.

dish: USDA prime steaks broiled with salt and pepper; cash or check only
w: Akron's frozen-in-time 1935 steakhouse — neon sign, phone booth, Sputnik chandeliers — and the haunt of tour pros like Tiger Woods during Firestone weeks. No. 1 Best Restaurant in the 330 (with sister Kingfish), Akron Life 330 Flavor Awards 2026.

dish: The MoFo — double bacon cheeseburger (Food Network's 'The Best Thing I Ever Ate'), with 64 beers on tap
w: Downtown Kent's bar-and-grill since 1937 and the town's standing answer to 'where should we eat': Best Restaurant in Portage County in Akron Life's 2026 Flavor Awards and a perennial KentWired Best of Kent winner.

dish: Diner breakfast with the big 'side' of bacon, nearly everything under $10
w: North Hill's no-frills counter diner, 30-plus years on Home Ave — Reader's Digest named it Ohio's most iconic diner and Signal Akron readers voted it Best Breakfast/Brunch 2026.

dish: Old-school red-sauce Italian and pizza from a 1940s Akron restaurant family
w: The Parasson family's restaurant traces to 1940s downtown Akron and Tonyo's Pizza in Barberton; the Beacon Journal calls a visit 'a trip to the past' and Akron Life readers ranked it No. 2 Italian in the 330 (2026).

dish: Griddle-browned hamburgers with Bob's special sauce, off the original 1931 grill
w: Akron's first hamburger joint (1931, Bob Holbrook), still using its original grill and fridge — a tiny counter that Ideastream calls the place that stays the same while restaurants come and go.

dish: Sushi and sashimi, pad thai and Szechuan from chef Luong Ly
w: The Ly family's downtown Canton bistro, nearly three decades in — first-named on the Canton Repository foodie panel's 11 best Stark County restaurants and on Cleveland Magazine's Canton must-go list.

dish: Estate wines with brick-oven pizza and house-made gnocchi at The Bistro
w: A 55-acre Tuscan-style winery resort on Canton's north side — 30-plus wines, three restaurants, villas and a spa; The Bistro made the Canton Repository panel's 11 best in Stark County.

dish: Shish kabobs and the Arabic platter
w: Family-owned Middle Eastern supper house since 1970 — one of the Canton Repository foodie panel's 11 best Stark County restaurants.

address: 4490 Erie Ave N, Canal Fulton, OH 44614
dish: Dry-aged USDA prime steaks and Italian classics
w: Family-owned since 1991 beside the Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath — the Canton Repository foodie panel's pick for steak in Stark County.

dish: Scratch homestyle chicken dinners, noodles and Hartville Kitchen pies
w: Hartville's Amish-country family restaurant and bakery since 1966 — nostalgic, scratch-made, and on the Canton Repository panel's 11 best in Stark County.

dish: Curries with scratch-made yogurt and warm naan
w: Belden Village Indian kitchen named to the Canton Repository foodie panel's 11 best Stark County restaurants.

dish: B.O.R.I.S. the Crusher oatmeal imperial stout (GABF / World Beer Cup gold)
w: Fred Karm's 2006 east-Akron brewery and tasting room, whose barrel-aged imperial stouts made it a RateBeer top-20 brewer in the world (2012).

dish: Root beer-braised pulled pork; waffles with hot sauce and bourbon butter
w: Downtown Akron's imaginative comfort-food room near the Art Museum, profiled by Ohio Magazine and Cleveland Magazine.

dish: 13 gourmet grilled cheeses and Akron's deepest craft-beer list
w: A former indie-music venue on Main St near the University of Akron turned the area's best-loved craft-beer bar, with a grilled-cheese menu to match.

dish: The Uncle Rico — grilled roast beef, tater tots and chive cream cheese on a toasted bagel (one of 38 movie-named sandwiches)
w: Highland Square's movie-themed deli and bar, on Cleveland Magazine's Highland Square must-visit list and Akron Life's stuffed-sandwich roundup.

dish: 16 Belgian waffles, including the deep-fried, cinnamon-sugared Churro
w: Akron's homegrown waffle house, a Cleveland Magazine Highland Square pick and Akron Life's go-to for Sunday brunch.

dish: Organic-market café plates on the 100-ft wraparound balcony
w: Akron's natural-foods market with a second-floor café and wraparound balcony over Highland Square — Signal Akron readers' 2026 Best Outdoor Dining.

dish: Scratch European breads and croissants; chef-driven brunch
w: Marine-veteran pastry chef Michael Bruno's 2009 café — No. 6 on Yelp's national Top 100 Brunch Spots (2024, per WKYC) and a Cleveland Magazine, Scene and Akron Life favorite.

dish: 25-plus tiki cocktails with house syrups and fresh juice
w: A shipwreck-themed tiki bar behind a carved cedar door, moved from Hudson to Front St in 2022.

dish: Farm-to-table house-ground burgers and 300-plus bourbons
w: Butcher-shop-meets-bourbon-bar in Cuyahoga Falls, profiled by Akron Life and on Cleveland Magazine's Falls best list.

dish: Creative small plates and luxury cocktails in an underground speakeasy
w: The Farmer's Rail's moody downstairs sibling — No. 1 Best New Restaurant in Akron Life's 2026 330 Flavor Awards.

dish: Contemporary American plates with floor-to-ceiling views over the Cuyahoga falls
w: Chef Beau Schmidt's riverside dining room in the Sheraton Suites; Schmidt was Akron Life readers' 2026 Best Chef and Best Restaurateur.

dish: New York-style pizza by the slice
w: Kent's slice shop for 30-plus years — KentWired Best of Kent pizza four years running and the Plain Dealer's Best Pizza in Portage County (2016).

dish: Weekend diner breakfasts and late-night burgers
w: Edge-of-downtown Kent café, KentWired readers' Best Breakfast and an Akron Life Kent pick.
